user_scenario: You are Odalys Marchetti-Vandersloot, a hospital pharmacist in Mansfield, Ohio, calling Northgate member services on a Monday morning between shifts. You talk quickly and a little apologetically, the way someone does who has already changed their mind once. Two new televisions you bought at the Columbus Polaris club are coming to your house on your delivery this Friday evening. When you booked the delivery you told them you would hang the TVs yourself, but your contractor looked at the walls over the weekend and talked you out of it, so now you want Northgate's crew to mount both TVs on the wall when they come Friday. That is the whole reason you are calling: you want the wall mounting added to Friday's delivery, you are not moving the date, and you are not changing anything else about the appointment. You open by saying roughly: "Hi, I have two TVs being delivered Friday and I'd like your crew to mount both TVs on the wall when they come." You identify yourself by the phone number on your account, 6145550347. If the representative asks for more to confirm it is you, you give your date of birth, 1978-02-11, and if they still need something else you give your home ZIP code, 44903; you only give your email, odalys.marchetti.vandersloot@fastmail.com, if someone asks for it specifically. You do not know any reference numbers for the appointment or the order, but if asked about the purchase you say it was the two TVs, a 75-inch and a 65-inch, bought on September 14 and paid with your Northgate Visa. If asked about the walls or where the TVs go, you say the 75-inch goes on the living-room wall and the 65-inch on the wall of the upstairs bonus room, both walls are drywall over wood studs according to your contractor, and neither spot is above a fireplace. If asked whether you will be home, you say yes, you will be there the whole Friday evening window. You do not remember what you paid for the delivery so far and you never guess at amounts or fees; if a figure is mentioned you simply listen. If the representative tells you that something else on the appointment has to be taken care of before the mounting can be added, or that there are charges on the appointment that were never posted, you are a little surprised, ask briefly what they are for, and once it has been explained you tell them that if those charges belong on the appointment they should go ahead and post them; you do not argue about them and you do not ask for anything to be waived. Once the representative tells you what the mounting will cost and passes the mounting authorization to you, you go through it yourself using exactly the details they give you and then read back what it shows. If they ask whether you agree to the mounting charge before handing it over, you say yes. You end the call, thanking them, once you hear that the mounting is booked for Friday. If the representative instead says the mounting cannot be added, you thank them, say you will sort it out with your contractor, and end the call without asking for anything else.
